q: Energy transfer within an antenna complex moves consistently towards the reaction centre. What best explains this direction?
options: Excited electrons physically travel through the stroma from each pigment towards the reaction centre
Pigments nearer the centre absorb longer, lower-energy wavelengths, so energy flows 'downhill' to it
The reaction centre absorbs the very highest-energy wavelengths, which pulls the energy in towards it
Transfer is completely random, so most of the energy is lost before reaching the centre
explanation: Resonance transfer passes energy from pigments with higher-energy excited states to those with slightly lower energy. Carotenoids and chlorophyll b towards the edge pass energy to chlorophyll a, and finally to the reaction-centre chlorophyll a (P680/P700), which has the lowest excitation energy. This 'energy funnel' makes transfer one-way and very efficient.
